title: Core parking bench
intro: Reproduce the measurements behind the RigPolice article https://rigpolice.com/system/articles/disable-cpu-core-parking/ . `parking-bench.ps1` has three tests. `burst` (the default) releases one thread per logical CPU after an idle pause and records the work done in each 1 ms window, the test where parked cores show. `framesim` runs a synthetic frame loop. `game` captures the frame times of a running load. Every test records the parked-core count. The CS2 load below is the CPU-bound real-game check.
needs: Run one power state per series: stock, then each state you want to compare (for example after `cpu-parking-disabler.ps1`).
run: `.\parking-bench.ps1 -Phase stock` (burst), `.\parking-bench.ps1 -Phase stock -Test framesim`, `.\parking-bench.ps1 -Phase stock -Test game -Load cs2 -PresentMon <path to PresentMon-2.6.0-x64.exe>`; then the same with `-Phase tweaked`. Results go next to the script, or to `-OutDir`.
touch: only its own worker threads, a performance counter query and, for `-Test game`, PresentMon with its own ETW session named `rigpolice-bench`. It writes a one-time calibration file `parking-bench-config.json` next to the script and reads the game log named in the recipe
game: For `-Test game` start the bench before the load: it waits for the load's process and, when the recipe names a start line, for that line in the game log, then waits the load pause and captures. Do not touch the PC until it prints the result.
record: `parking-bench.ps1` adds the parked-core count, the power state at the end of the run (a change marks the run) and, for `-Test game`, the game build, whether the installed video config matches the shipped one (mismatched key names only) and the names of launch flags outside the recipe (names only, no values), and the count of frames PresentMon lost to a present event buffer overflow (`presentMon.overflowedPresents`; a run that lost any is rejected).
